layout:
Pure: games.bin, a struct-of-arrays binary, little-endian.

Header (20 bytes): magic "LGG2" | n uint32 | dim uint32 | scale float32 | n_maps uint32.
Then n-long columns back to back, widest first so every column is aligned:
  appid int32 | reviews uint32 | year int16 (0 unknown)
  | for each map in games.json "maps" order: x float16 | y float16 | z float16 | cluster int16 (fine cluster id, -1 absent)
  | split uint8 (0 past, 1 future) | novelty_pct uint8 (0-100) | positive_pct uint8
  | vec int8 (n x dim, row-major)
A game that is not in a map has x = y = z = NaN and cluster -1 in that map.
Every game in a map has a fine cluster (no noise). clusters_<map>.json gives each fine cluster's
"parent" (coarse id), so a game's coarse cluster is the parent of its fine one.
vec[i, j] * scale / 127 is the j-th component of game i's unit 64-d PCA vector.
Row order matches the "names" list in games.json.
